content.text: Plan Your Trip to Sydney: Best of Sydney TourismWhat is Travelers’ Choice Best of the Best?This award is our highest recognition and is presented annually to those businesses that are the Best of the Best on Tripadvisor, those that earn excellent reviews from travelers and are ranked in the top 1% of properties worldwide.Learn moreSave this place to a Trip, where you can track your faves and get personalized picks as you plan.Sydney is a place that’s really got it all: It’s a sunny, modern city, right smack in the middle of nature, where gallery-hopping, surfing, and fine dining can all happen before the sun goes down. Start with the views: Take the cliff-top coastal walk along the city's southern coast, where you’ll pass by beaches, rock pools, and lush parks. Then there’s the world-famous Sydney Opera House—jutting up like a huge sailboat—anchoring iconic Sydney Harbour. It’s also worth seeing the city from the top down; the views from the Sydney Tower Eye observatory are nothing less than epic.Discover your perfect SydneyLooking for places to stay, eat, or explore?Essential SydneyPick a category to filter your recsThings to doPlaces to stayFood & drinkTravel AdviceWhen to visitJanuary8 days of rainWettest monthLess busyLeast busy monthItineraries to help you planCreated by AI, guided by insights from our community. Learn moreHow to do Sydney in 4 daysSurf lessons, free museums, and a royal shopping tripRead onDig into Sydney and beyondStories, tips, and guidesItineraries from real travelersWhat to see and do, from people who have been thereYou don’t want to miss these saltwater pools in SydneyThe only thing better than Sydney's famous beaches are its sparkling saltwater ocean pools. With wild surf and rip currents, saltwater pools are a safer (and slightly more chic) alternative to the open ocean and they are beloved by tourists and locals alike. As a local Sydneysider and avid ocean swimmer (who can't resist an afternoon dip!), I've done my own deep dive into the best saltwater pools in Sydney. If there were a crown jewel of ocean pools, it would be Bondi Icebergs. I love people-watching here or bringing along my camera, as Icebergs is one of the most beautiful saltwater pools in the country. The contrast of the turquoise surf lapping against the bright white pool deck is honestly iconic. It's one of the few saltwater pools in Sydney that isn't free but worth the small charge. Avoid Thursdays, when Icebergs is closed for cleaning. This unique, triangle-shaped pool is a must-see on any visit to Manly Beach. You'll come across it on the Manly to Shelly Beach walk. Being on the smaller side, this attractive pool is perfect for kids. It was built by residents in 1929 and is famous for its whimsical sculpture, Oceanides. You're also just around the bend from Shelly Beach, my favorite snorkeling spot in Sydney. Bronte Baths feels so quintessentially Aussie—it features a 30-meter pool carved out of sandstone rock, along with a splash and play area for kids. If you don't want to pay for admission to Icebergs, this is a top free alternative that offers very similar views. Bronte Baths tend to be on the chiller side, so I'm always sure to swim with my rash guard (highly recommended for sun protection, too).A short walk from Coogee Beach is Wylie's Baths saltwater pool. Coming here makes me smile because it feels like stepping back in time. Dating back to 1907, it's one of the last remaining ocean baths, complete with a high boardwalk offering epic views. And if you're up for a day of relaxation, it's also one of the most scenic spots in Sydney for a yoga or Pilates class!If you're on Sydney's Lower North Shore, Maccullum Seawater Pool is one of the most picturesque places to swim. Set in Cremorne Point, this small but scenic ocean pool can get popular on weekends, with sunbathers vying for space on the pool's inviting timber decks. However, it's easily accessed from the Circular Quay ferry, so there's no need to stress over parking spaces. I recommend stopping by for a sunset swim and enjoying some fantastic views of the Harbour Bridge!You'll often see this iconic saltwater pool in aerial photography of Sydney, but it's just as impressive in real life! With a 50-meter lap pool and a splash area for little ones, this ocean bath almost has it all—changing rooms, bathrooms, and parking—it just lacks lap lane markers, which may annoy some serious swimmers. Check with the Northern Beaches Council website for opening information — it's closed on select Mondays for cleaning.Near Cronulla, you'll discover Shelly Beach Rock Pool, a large ocean bath popular with young families. With both stairs and a long ramp, this pool also scores points for accessibility. While the large pool makes it ideal for swimming laps, I also like that Shelly Beach Rock Pool has a spacious beach and grass lawn, perfect for picnics. Note there's no natural shade here, so bring along your beach umbrella. Use the bus, train, or ferry to get where you need to be. The city itself, though it can be hilly, is great for walking.Lyn DDownload Tripview App to your smartphone for the latest public transport schedule.Africa TouristAustralians do not tip. People working in service industries are well paid by world standards, and so do not feel obligated to tip.DONNA063Sydney has a lot of wonderful places to visit that suit all ages and tastes. It has one of the most beautiful harbours in the world with the Sydney Harbour Bridge and The Sydney Opera House as the main focal points. The Blue Mountains are a three-hour train ride and is well worth a visit.2gnomesinparisSydney is a beautiful city to explore. The harbour is so pretty with lots to do. There are many things to see and do around Sydney as well as wonderful shopping. The cafes and restaurants are amazing! Easy to get around, you can walk to most things. Our amazing beaches are a short bus or ferry ride from the city. Kids will love the zoo and the view over the harbour from the zoo is to die for! The air is clean, the sky is blue, the harbour is magnificent!Michael NSydney has become a cosmopolitan city compared favorably with other great cities of the world. Centered around its magnificent harbour, there are many attractions and experiences to be enjoyed.What is the best way to get there?flyingSydney Kingsford Smith International Airport (SYD) is Australia’s busiest airport, with daily flights to/from major global destinations on dozens of airlines.Do I need a visa?When is the best time to visit?March to May: The best times to visit Sydney are between March and May and September and November. You’ll find more comfortable temperatures and fewer crowds — which means you can likely nab better prices on airfare, too.But if you want to warm up with the masses from winter back home, the average daily temperatures in January can hit highs of 30°C/86°F and lows around 20°C/67°F.Get aroundPublic TransitSydney has a great public transportation network. Be sure to download the TripView app for train, ferry, bus and light rail schedules.Buying an Opal Card is another must for getting around Sydney as it’s the easiest way to pay for public transit. For more info, visit here.trainsThe Sydney Metro system is still under construction, but it currently has one line running from Chatswood to Tallawong. You can also get local and regional train service on NSW TrainLink and Sydney Trains to/from Central Station.tramsThere are two tram lines in Sydney that can also get you around town.busSydney’s massive bus network operates until midnight usually, and there are many hubs around the city.ferriesThe nine routes of Sydney Ferries are a great way to get around and see the city. bikesThough traffic can be intense, Sydney has bike lanes and many bike-rentals companies.taxisTaxis are readily available in Sydney for hailing and booking via the NSW Taxi Council.ridesharesUber can be booked via its app on your smartphone.On the groundWhat is the timezone?Australian EasternWhat are the voltage/plug types?220-240 volts ACWhat is the currency?Australian dollarAre ATMs readily accessible?Yes.Are credit cards widely accepted?Yes.How much do I tip?Tipping is not expected in Australia, however, a tip for exceptional service is always appreciated.Restaurants/barsAgain, it’s not customary, but you can add between 5 and 10% if you are super happy.HotelsA few AUDs would be appreciated for anyone who helps with your bags and the housekeeping staff.TaxisRounding up to the nearest AUD is typical.Tour guidesIf your guide was particularly fun or interesting, 10 AUD would suffice.Are there local customs I should know?DrinkingThe legal drinking age in Sydney is 18.GreetingsHandshakes are a customary greeting in Sydney.Public transitOffer your seat to people who are old, pregnant or have mobility issues.Sydney travel tipsThese questions and answers were created by AI, using the most common questions travelers ask in the forums.Opal Card UsageAccording to forum posts, travelers can use an Opal card for easy access to multiple modes of public transportation in Sydney, including trains, buses, and ferries. The card is free, and top-ups can be done at newsagents or using machines at stations.Contactless PaymentsFor many users, contactless credit cards offer the same benefits as the Opal card, including fare caps and discounts. This method is especially recommended to avoid leftover funds on an Opal card, as unused balances are not refunded but remain valid for seven years.Public Transportation CoverageSome travelers noted that Sydney's public transport system is extensive, covering major areas and attractions efficiently. Trains from the airport go directly to Central Station and Circular Quay, and buses serve routes across the city. The B-Line bus and regular ferries, like the one to Manly, provide scenic and practical transport options for both daily commutes and tourist explorations.Airport ConnectivityTravelers have called out the train as a quick and direct option from Sydney International Airport to the city center, emphasizing its convenience over buses, which may involve transfers and longer travel times.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Top Hotel PicksAccording to forum posts, the Park Hyatt is highly recommended for its location and quality, offering views of the Harbour and the Opera House. Travelers have called out the Shangri-La for its luxurious suites, though some have reported being underwhelmed by their stay. The Four Seasons has been noted for its significant improvements and competitive pricing after renovations.Alternative ChoicesFor many users, the Langham and the Pullman Quay Grand are also favorable options, with the former being praised for its less conferencey feel and the latter for its large rooms with balcony suites. The Meriton chain, especially for its penthouse options, is preferred by some for its locations like The Rocks.Budget-Friendly OptionsThe Great Southern Hotel and various Meriton properties were mentioned for those looking for more budget-friendly options. These establishments offer clean, comfortable accommodations and are conveniently located near public transportation, making them ideal for travelers looking to explore Sydney without breaking the bank.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Family-friendly AttractionsAccording to forum posts, family-friendly attractions in Sydney include Taronga Zoo, Luna Park, and the Sydney Opera House. These locations offer engaging activities suitable for children and provide a comprehensive experience of Sydney’s cultural and recreational highlights.Outdoor ActivitiesFor outdoor enthusiasts, some travelers suggested the Bondi to Coogee coastal walk, which includes opportunities for swimming and surf lessons. Additionally, the Royal National Park was mentioned as a great spot for a day out, offering bushwalking and picturesque picnic areas.Interactive and Educational ExperiencesTravelers have called out the Australian Museum and the Powerhouse Museum for their interactive exhibits that can be particularly enjoyable and educational for children. These museums offer a mix of history, science, and technology.Unique ExperiencesFor a unique experience, taking a ferry from Circular Quay for a day trip to Manly was recommended. This trip offers stunning views of the harbour and a chance to explore less crowded beaches, which could be a more relaxed alternative to the often busy Bondi Beach.Events and Seasonal AttractionsDuring specific times, such as Easter, families might enjoy the Royal Easter Show, which features agricultural displays, amusement rides, and food stalls, providing fun for all ages.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Transport OptionsSome travelers recommended taking a train from Central Station to Katoomba for a day trip to the Blue Mountains, highlighting its convenience. From Katoomba, options such as public buses or the hop-on hop-off (HOHO) bus are available to navigate the area, allowing access to major attractions like the Three Sisters and Scenic World.Self-Driving ConsiderationsFor those preferring flexibility, self-driving was suggested as a viable option. This allows visitors to explore the Blue Mountains at their own pace and access various hiking trails and viewpoints, although parking can be challenging at popular spots during peak times.Tour-Based VisitsAlternatively, several users mentioned the availability of guided day tours, which often include transportation from Sydney and stops at key attractions. These tours can be convenient for those who prefer structured itineraries and include additional stops like wildlife parks.Local InsightsAccording to forum posts, staying overnight was recommended to fully appreciate the area, although a day trip can offer a good overview of the Blue Mountains’ scenic spots if time is limited.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Location and General PreferencesAccording to forum posts, travelers prefer accommodations near Circular Quay due to its central location and easy access to major attractions in Sydney. The area is favored for its proximity to transport hubs and scenic views of the Sydney Harbour.Hotel OptionsSome travelers suggested the Pullman Quay Grand as a top choice for its location and views, though it can be pricey. The Four Seasons is noted for being steps away from Circular Quay, offering convenience although some users found the rooms small. The InterContinental is another recommended option, with slightly better room sizes but a slight uphill walk from the Quay.Apartments and Budget OptionsFor those looking for apartment-style accommodations, Quay West is a popular choice, offering larger spaces and sometimes cheaper rates compared to Quay Grand. Budget-conscious travelers mentioned the YHA for its location and rooftop balcony, providing a more economical stay without sacrificing too much convenience.ConsiderationsTravelers have called out that prices for accommodations can vary greatly based on the time of year and specific events, suggesting flexibility and early booking as key to securing a good deal.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Available Cruise OptionsAccording to forum posts, travelers have various options for experiencing Sydney Harbour. Some users recommend taking public ferries as a cost-effective way to enjoy the views. These ferries cover significant parts of the harbour and are ideal for sightseeing and photography. Popular ferry trips mentioned include the Manly and Watsons Bay routes.Specialized Cruise ExperiencesFor a more structured tour, the Captain Cook Cruises offer a range of options. Travelers have called out specific ships like Matilda 3, John Cadman II, and Sydney 2000, which are part of the Harbour of Light Parade and Exclusion Zone during New Year's Eve. These cruises often include live entertainment and provide excellent views of the fireworks.Dinner CruisesOn the topic of dinner cruises, while some travelers suggest avoiding them due to mediocre food quality, there are still several mentioned for those interested. The Showboat Dinner Cruise offers a 3-course meal and entertainment. The Clearview Glass Boat Signature Dinner Cruise provides a chef-prepared three-course dinner with panoramic harbour views.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Beach RecommendationsFor many users, Manly Beach is highly recommended due to its ferry access from Sydney, making it easy to combine city sightseeing with beach relaxation. It offers a blend of ocean and harbor beaches and is rich in amenities like cafes and shops. Another popular choice is Bondi Beach, known for its vibrant atmosphere and extensive beachfront. It also serves as a starting point for the scenic Bondi to Coogee coastal walk.Quieter OptionsTravelers have called out Cronulla and Bundeena for those seeking quieter beach experiences. Cronulla provides a balance with good local eateries and less crowded conditions, alongside easy train access to Sydney. Bundeena, nestled in the Royal National Park, offers a more secluded environment with beautiful natural surroundings, although it is a bit farther and requires a ferry and train ride or a drive to reach.Alternative Beach TownsAccording to forum posts, other beach towns like Kiama and the Northern Beaches offer laid-back vibes with various amenities. Kiama is known for its picturesque views and less crowded beaches, while the Northern Beaches area is highlighted for its relaxed atmosphere and accessibility via public transport, making it a practical choice for visitors staying in Sydney.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Terminal Transfer OptionsFor travelers needing to transfer between terminals at Sydney Airport, there are several options available. According to forum posts, if you are transferring between Qantas flights, there is a seamless transfer service provided by Qantas that includes a free shuttle bus from the international terminal (T1) to the domestic terminal (T3). This service is described as quick and efficient.Bus and Train ServicesFor those not flying with Qantas or needing to transfer to Terminal 2, the TBus service and trains are available. The Sydney Airport website provides details on these services, and the TBus is mentioned as a free option for travelers. Additionally, the transfer process involves following specific signs and possibly passing by landmarks such as a McDonald's, according to some travelers.Transfer AdviceSome travelers have advised allowing ample time for transfers between terminals, especially considering the distance and security procedures. This is particularly important if the transfer involves re-checking luggage or additional security checks.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Peak hotel prices generally start between December and February.
